newsitem.title: IRAN: Quake hits northwest Iran, causes casualties.
newsitem.headline: Quake hits northwest Iran, causes casualties.

text.p: A strong earthquake hit northwestern Iran on Friday, causing unspecified casualties and damage, the Iranian news agency IRNA said.

It said the quake, measuring about six degrees on the Richter scale, jolted areas outside Ardabil, a provincial capital near the border with Azerbaijan, for about 15 seconds and sent residents running from their homes.
"Based on reports available, the quake has caused loss of property and casaulties in certain suburban villages," IRNA said without giving further details.
The earthquake struck at 4.31 p.m. (1301 GMT) and was followed by several aftershocks, the agency said.
Two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale killed at least 79 people and injured 260 in northeastern Iran in early February.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in a densely populated area near the Caspian coast in 1990.
